name: Divine Exemplar
body:
You are touched by the divine, its considerable influence within you demonstrated by the means of extraordinary gifts. Many believe these to be signs not just of divine favor, but of your own divine heritage, proof that the blood of the gods or their powerful representatives may flow through your veins. Regardless, you are instinctively drawn to a life of adventure where you can both discover your true potential and pursue your sacred destiny.

Parent Classes Medium and oracle. The divine exemplar combines mechanics from both of these classes, but it defines a new character concept—that of a hero embodying legendary abilities. Like a medium, the divine exemplar has a lot of versatility in design, but because they embody only one legend (the equivalent of a medium’s spirits)—which is set in stone at 1st level—you build solely around that singular specialization, greatly reducing the class’s complexity. Additionally, the medium’s occult features are replaced by divine revelations from an oracle mystery. This allows you to create a burgeoning immortal—a character that feels infused with divine energy, whether from having an actual blood relation to a deity or demigod, or from just inheriting some mythic gift.

Alignment Any.

Hit Die 1d8.

Starting Wealth 4d6 × 10 (average 140 gp).

Role Although divine exemplars channel divine power, they do so intuitively. Not all of them serve a deity, nor are they strictly reliant upon their deity if they do follow one. Divine exemplars are versatile, with most able to perform well in combat, social situations, and many specialized roles. Depending upon your choice of legend, mystery, and spells, you can further specialize to excel in the role you most wish to exemplify.

Class Skills

Your class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int). In addition, you receive additional class skills depending upon your mystery.

Skill Ranks per Level 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the divine exemplar class.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

You are proficient with all simple weapons, light armor, medium armor, and shields (except tower shields). Some of your class features grant additional proficiencies.

Spell Casting

You can cast a small number of divine spells drawn from the medium spell list; as a divine caster, you need a divine focus if the spell requires one. To learn or cast a spell, you must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell’s level. You can cast any spell you know without preparing it ahead of time. The saving throw DC against one of your spells is equal to 10 + the spell level + your Charisma modifier.

You can cast only a certain number of spells of each level per day. Your base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Spells per Day. In addition, you receive bonus spells per day if you have a high Charisma score.

Your selection of spells is limited. At 1st level, you know two 0-level spells of your choice. At each new level, you learn one or more new spells, as indicated on Table: Spells Known. Unlike your spells per day, the number of spells you know is not affected by your Charisma score; the numbers on Table: Spells Known are fixed. At 5th level and every 3 levels thereafter, you can learn a single new spell in place of one you already know. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and you must choose whether to swap the spell at the same time you gain new spells known for the level.

Orisons You learn a number of orisons, or 0-level spells, as noted on Table: Spells Known. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they don’t consume slots and can be used again.

Legend (Su)

You serve as the embodiment of a powerful archetype—a legend in the making, echoing the brave actions of adventurers of the past. This functions similarly to the way a medium channels a spirit, except that you choose one legend at 1st level, and once chosen it is always active and never changes.

At 1st level, you gain your legend’s listed lesser power. You gain its intermediate power at 6th level, its greater power at 12th level, and its supreme power at 18th level.

Destiny (Su)

In addition to granting you power, the unyielding momentum of your legendary destiny impedes you in other ways. Each day, after you complete 8 hours of sleep, you begin the day with 1 point of destiny. If your destiny ever drops below 1 point, you lose contact with your legend, and you lose any powers your legend grants. Certain abilities allow you to gain additional power in exchange for gaining additional points of destiny—but this comes at a price.

With each point of destiny you gain, your sense of self gradually becomes suppressed and you begin to succumb to the impulses that drive your legend. This causes your specific penalties (as listed in your legend’s entry) to increase. However, you also gain a bonus on saving throws against all mind-affecting effects equal to 1/3 the number of points of destiny that you possess.

You cannot willingly allow your destiny to exceed a number greater than 1/2 your divine exemplar level (minimum 1) + your highest ability score bonus. However, some effects my cause your destiny to involuntarily exceed this value.

Legend Bonus (Su)

Depending on the legend you choose at 1st level, you gain a bonus on certain checks and to certain statistics. At 1st-level, the bonus granted by your legend is +1. It increases by 1 at 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, to a maximum of +6 at 20th level.

Legend Surge (Su)

After failing a d20 roll that was modified by your legend bonus, you can accept 1 additional point of destiny in order to add 1d6 to the check’s result without taking an action. This can cause the check to succeed instead of fail. You must be conscious and aware to use this ability, and you can use this ability at most once per round. At 10th level, your legend surge die increases to 1d8, and at 20th level it increases to 1d10.

Mystery

Like an oracle, you draw upon a divine mystery to grant you certain spells and powers. This mystery also grants additional class skills and other special abilities. Your mystery can represent a devotion to one ideal, prayers to deities that support the concept, or an inborn divine calling that cannot be denied. For example, if you have the wind mystery, you may find yourself drawn to the power and fury of ferocious storms, called to embrace the cracking thunder and howling wind—wherein you feel both a divine presence and a sort of kinship.

Regardless of its source, your mystery manifests in a number of ways as you gain levels. You must pick a mystery upon taking your first level of divine exemplar. Once made, this choice cannot be changed.

The list of mysteries available to a divine exemplar is the same as the choices available to an oracle. Unlike an oracle, your mystery does not give you access to a list of bonus spells.

Revelation

At 2nd level and every three levels thereafter (5th, 8th, and so on) until 17th level, you uncover a new secret about your mystery that grants you powers and abilities. You must select a revelation from the list of revelations available to your mystery. You use your divine exemplar level as your effective oracle level. If a revelation is chosen at a later level, you gain all of the abilities and bonuses granted by that revelation based on your current level.

Unless otherwise noted, activating the power of a revelation is a standard action.

Legend Bonus Feat

At 3rd level and every 4 levels thereafter, you receive one bonus feat, chosen from a list specific to each legend. You must meet the prerequisites for these bonus feats.

Master of Your Own Destiny

At 7th level, you have learned special techniques and prayers that allow you to reduce the impact of your destiny. Once per day as a free action, you can suspend all penalties associated with your destiny for 1 round.

You gain an additional use of this ability at 13th level, and again at 19th level.

At 13th level, you can expend both uses at once, as a free action, to have the effect last for an entire minute. At 19th level, you can expend all three uses at one time, as a free action, to have the effect last for 10 minutes.

Final Revelation

At 20th level, you learn the final revelation about your mystery, granting you amazing powers and abilities. The nature of these bonuses depends upon your chosen mystery.
